title: How do we draw the three views of joined cubes?
description: Identical cubes are joined, and the board draws the front view, the top view and the side view of one combination. It draws a square for every cube that can be seen, leaves out the cube hidden behind another, and then checks that widths and heights agree across the views.
teaching_notes: One idea: each view has one square for every cube you can see, and a cube hidden behind another adds none. Watch for students who draw a square for every cube in every view.

source: Figure it Out (shadows and views, question 1)
video_script.why: The child looks straight at the cubes from three sides, draws what can be seen, and checks that the three views agree.
video_script.substitution: Draw one square for every cube seen from that side, then compare widths and heights of the views.
video_script.anchor: identical cubes joined face to face: three in a row with a fourth on top of the left cube, and three empty frames for the front, top and side views
video_script.payoff_line: Draw one square for every cube you can see in each view

final_answer.value: one square for every cube you can see in each view, matching widths and heights across the views; here the front view has 4 squares, the top view 3 squares and the side view 2 squares
final_answer.spoken: one square for every cube you can see in each view, with matching widths and heights

hold_back: Answer: one square for every cube you can see in each view; front view 4 squares, top view 3 squares, side view 2 squares
never_show: a top view with four squares marked as right
maths_rules: stand-in combination: 3 cubes in a row and a 4th cube on top of the left cube
front view: 3 squares in a row and 1 square on top of the left one, 3 + 1 = 4 squares
top view: the top cube hides the cube below it, so 3 squares in a row
side view: the 3 cubes of the row hide behind one another, so one column of 2 squares
check: front and top views share the width of 3 squares; front and side views share the height of 2 squares
video_script.design: Three frames for the front, top and side views beside the cubes. Each frame is filled in turn and the widths and heights are lined up at the end.
open_questions: The combinations of the book are pictures that are not in the extracted text, so the video works one combination of the same kind (three cubes in a row and a fourth on top of the left cube) and gives the method for the others.
